TrueMark · the closer look

All nine, mapped

The nine design points from the critique, plus the stop-start rhythm, as one plan. Each picture flips between how it is now and how it would look.

The mock-ups are drawn over the real page: the changes are pasted on for the pictures, so nothing in the app has changed yet. The shadow and the phone vial’s size are close guesses.

In one breath

A quieter film. Semax is the star, the words sit on the scene, and one thin line shows where you are. Something always moves while you scroll, and nothing moves when you stop.

What stays

The room with five vials on pedestals, Semax’s real label, the real lot and its real certificate, and the big 99.78%.

The nine

Numbered as in the critique. The numbers also mark where each one shows in the pictures below.

1

Point 1: Too many controls

Three buttons, “Next detail”, “Scroll to explore” and two counters. It reads like a video player.

One thin line: the chapter’s name, how far along you are, and two small words, Skip and Motion. Clicking the line still jumps to a chapter, and the keyboard still works.

MediumReady

2

Point 2: The same white card every chapter

It’s the heaviest thing on screen and it outweighs the vial.

The words sit straight on the scene, like the headline. Only the real things keep a box: the Verify field, the lot record, the certificate.

MediumYour call: how far

3

Point 3: Pointer lines and big numbered circles

Lines cross the label and it looks like a diagram.

Small corner marks, the same ones the certificate uses, frame each detail on the label and glide to the next as you scroll. Nothing crosses the print.

MediumReady

4

Point 4: No shadow under the floating vial

It looks pasted on.

A soft shadow on its pedestal, wide and faint while the vial is high, firmer as it lands.

SmallReady

5

Point 5: Cut-off blurry vials along the bottom

Stray colour under the controls.

While the camera is close on Semax, the other four vials step back into the room. They come back for the finale.

SmallReady

6

Point 6: The certificate is too small to read

The highlight on 99.78% is tiny, so the proof doesn’t land.

A small reading glass slides over the certificate’s own print: 99.78% in the lab’s type, large and sharp. Our photo of the page is sharp enough for it.

MediumReady

7

Point 7: Every headline is the same two-beat line

By the fourth one it feels repetitive.

These are the client’s words, so it’s their call. My suggestion: keep the two-beat line for the opening and the finale, and one plain line for each chapter between. One more: “Follow each marker” may want a word changed once the numbered markers go.

SmallClient’s call

8

Point 8: Finale text sits on the pedestals

Two layers of small text overlap the lot labels.

The four principles move below the room, as the first thing after the film. The finale shows the five vials and their lots clean.

SmallReady

9

Point 9: On a phone, the card and controls cover 60%

The vial gets squeezed.

One line instead of two rows, only the detail being read, and the vial about a fifth bigger. This comes with 1 and 2.

MediumComes with 1 and 2

See it, chapter by chapter

Flip each picture between Mapped and Now.

The rhythm

The motion fault still open from the critique. Now, the picture stands still through the whole label and the whole certificate (each more than a screen of scrolling), then the vial going home, the room darkening, the camera and the certificate all move at once. Mapped, the corner marks glide between the label’s details and the reading glass between the findings, and the vial lands before the certificate comes forward. No still stretch is longer than about half a screen. The line shows seven stops (the six chapters and the finale) instead of eleven.

The order I’d build it

Each step is checked in Chrome and Safari, by keyboard and screen reader, with motion off and on a phone, then saved locally and sent to you as frames.

  1. The room: the shadow, the clean bottom edge, and the finale’s principles below the room (4, 5, 8).small
  2. One line in place of the controls, on desktop and phone (1, 9).medium
  3. Words on the scene and the phone layout (2, 9).medium
  4. Corner marks, the reading glass and the new rhythm (3, 6). The biggest step: it re-times the film.large
  5. Headlines (7), once the client answers.waits

Calls

Yours

  • Go on all of it, in this order?
  • Words on the scene all the way, keeping boxes only for the three real things (the Verify field, the record, the certificate)?
  • Seven stops on the line instead of eleven?

The client’s

  • The headlines (7), and “Follow each marker”.
  • Optional: a sharper photo of the Semax vial, if they want a reading glass on the label too. Ours is sharp at today’s size but not when magnified.

Everything new moves like the rest of the film, slid and faded and never redrawn, so it stays smooth.
